first_impression.reaction: Mykonos is on our list but I'm half worried it's the 'party island' and our friends will think it's try-hard. The opener is calm and practical. It splits the island into five areas and gives me a way to sort them: 'The right one depends on how many guests you are inviting, the ceremony you want and how your guests will move around the island.' No 'say I do in paradise'. The capacity takeaway (25 up to 800) tells me I can cross things off fast for 60 to 90. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Several venues have a chapel of their own, but the rules differ, from religious, civil and symbolic weddings at Grecotel Mykonos Lolita to religious weddings at Mykonos Grand only when both partners are Christian Orthodox.
journey.reaction: Neither of us is Orthodox, so this saved me from falling for the Mykonos Grand chapel and finding out later. Exactly the fine print I want up front.

journey.section: Mykonos wedding venues at a glance (table)
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: Good, it doesn't feel like a paid 'best of'. But the Exclusive use column is 'Not published' nine times out of ten, and capacity is blank for four. For 60 to 90 I can only really confirm Saint John, Petasos, the Elia hotels and maybe Mykonos Blu.

journey.quote: Add three questions to every list: is there a step-free route between rooms, ceremony and reception; what is the plan on a windy afternoon; and what time must the music stop?
journey.reaction: Step-free route is the grandparents question I wouldn't have thought to ask until it was too late. This is the paragraph I'd copy into our spreadsheet.

journey.quote: Anything this guide marks "Not published", from curfew to minimum nights, your Wedded Advisor confirms in writing with the venue before you commit, so [talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding-venues&utm_content=secondary).
journey.reaction: Said once, clearly, and it turns all those blanks into something someone else chases for me. That's the 'no spreadsheets for 18 months' promise I actually want.

journey.section: Choosing an area of the island
journey.quote: A simple rule: if guests want to be near town, start on the west coast. If you want the beach in every photograph, look south. If you want privacy and a chapel, look north.
journey.reaction: Screenshot for James. A clear opinion I can act on.

journey.section: Choosing an area of the island
journey.quote: Choose this coast if guests want evenings in town between wedding events.
journey.reaction: Useful, but nothing on the elephant in the room: is Mykonos Town in peak season a fun night out for our guests or a nightclub crush that Mum and Dad will hate? I'd want a line on that before I send this to them.

journey.quote: An open-air amphitheatre, and a complimentary evening shuttle to Mykonos Town for guests who want a night in town.
journey.reaction: Small practical detail that means I'm not organising taxis for 80 people. More of this, please.

journey.quote: [Mykonos Blu](https://www.grecotel.com/mykonosblu/weddings-mykonos/) hosts weddings and vow renewals on Psarou beach, "with the enchanting sunset as a backdrop", with dedicated wedding specialists and customised menus.
journey.reaction: I know it's the hotel's line, but opening the entry with 'enchanting sunset' plus 'sun kissed beach' at Katikies makes a few sections read like brochure copy. Not a deal-breaker; the bullets underneath are solid.

journey.quote: Up to 60 guests on the Ocean Balcony, and the wedding table and party for up to 120 in the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area.
journey.reaction: At 60 to 90 we'd be right on or over the balcony limit. Good that the number is there so I can see it straight away.

journey.quote: This is the only venue on the list that names civil weddings at its chapel, which matters if you want the legal ceremony and the setting in one place.
journey.reaction: Does 'civil wedding at the chapel' mean it's legally registered there, with an official present? Or is there still a town hall step? And capacity is 'Not published', so I don't know if 80 of us even fit.

journey.quote: The venue's own services include a physician and medical room during events, security with CCTV, and guest transfers that ZeNIT runs itself for up to 16 guests, with larger groups handled through its partners and transfers by sea also offered.
journey.reaction: A doctor on site with older guests in the heat is exactly my 'something goes wrong and no one is accountable' fear answered. Shame every venue doesn't get this level of detail.

journey.section: Getting to Mykonos for your wedding
journey.quote: Most venues do not publish a distance from the airport, so ask each for its transfer time before guests book.
journey.reaction: This is my number one worry, grandparents from the airport to the venue, and the answer is 'ask'. A bus stop and taxi rank won't cut it for 40-odd international guests landing on different flights. I need to know whether you organise transfers.

journey.quote: A date outside the summer months sits outside the heatwave and wildfire season.
journey.reaction: Heat and wildfire handled calmly with real actions, good. But which months, exactly? Late May? Early October? And are these hotels even open then? No month-by-month view to send Mum and Dad.

journey.quote: The full steps for marrying in Greece as Australians are in [our guide to Greece wedding venues](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues#getting-legally-married-in-greece-as-australians-in-brief).
journey.reaction: Clear on the CNI and recognition back home, which lawyer brain appreciates. But for anything Mykonos-specific I'm sent to another page. Fine, I'll click, but I'd have liked one line on where the civil step happens on the island.

journey.section: Shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person and AUD quotes hit two of my fears directly: being passed around strangers and currency surprises. Still doesn't say who is physically there on the day.

unanswered_questions: Is there a real Mykonos (or Greece) wedding you've planned, with venue and date, that I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests, half flying from Australia, which two or three of these ten would you actually shortlist?
Do you arrange airport transfers for guests, including older guests, or only advise on them?
Does a civil wedding at the Grecotel Mykonos Lolita chapel count as the legal marriage, and how many guests does that chapel hold?
Which months are these venues open for weddings, and which shoulder-season months would you recommend to avoid peak heat?
How busy and loud is Mykonos Town in peak season for guests who want a quiet evening?
Is our Wedded Advisor, or someone you are accountable for, physically on Mykonos on the wedding day?

turn_offs_found.turn_off: Clichés: fairytale, dream day, say I do in paradise
turn_offs_found.quote: [Mykonos Blu](https://www.grecotel.com/mykonosblu/weddings-mykonos/) hosts weddings and vow renewals on Psarou beach, "with the enchanting sunset as a backdrop", with dedicated wedding specialists and customised menus.
turn_offs_found.why: It's the hotel's own phrase, but leading an entry with 'enchanting sunset' (and 'sun kissed beach' at Katikies) is the brochure language I skim past and the sort of thing that makes Mykonos feel tacky to our friends. Leading with the facts and dropping or demoting the quote would fix it. Mild, not a deal-breaker.

would_share_with: James (partner): the at-a-glance table and the 'simple rule' paragraph, so we can rule areas in or out together
Mum and Dad (contributing): the heat and wildfire section and the ZeNIT on-site physician detail, to reassure them about the grandparents
James again: the three questions to add to every list (step-free route, wind plan, music curfew) as our checklist

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Mykonos venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right and not pushy, and the 'Not published, we confirm in writing' line makes the consultation feel useful rather than salesy. I'd still read one or two more posts and want to see a real wedding before I enquire, and I'd want the airport transfer question answered.

top_3_changes: Strengthen the airport section for guests: give whatever transfer times venues do publish and say plainly what to plan for older or long-haul guests, rather than ending on 'ask each for its transfer time'.

Clarify the Grecotel Mykonos Lolita civil-wedding line: whether a civil wedding at the chapel is the legal registration, or point to where the civil step happens, so 'legal ceremony and the setting in one place' doesn't leave a lawyer guessing.
Lead the Mykonos Blu and Katikies entries with facts, not the hotels' 'enchanting sunset' and 'sun kissed' lines, and add a short note on which shoulder-season months the venues are open.

open_questions.question: The Lolita line 'the only venue on the list that names civil weddings at its chapel, which matters if you want the legal ceremony and the setting in one place' may imply legal registration at the chapel. Worth checking with the planner SME that this wording doesn't overstate what the source says?
